symptom: The mirror workflow's 2026-10-22 15:03 UTC run re-created 40 mirrors of upstream issues that already had one (#1571-#1610; 31 duplicated open mirrors, 8 revived issues the maintainer had closed as completed), and the triage routine then classified the duplicates as new issues. Later, when upstream closed #280, the workflow closed the duplicate #1584 and left the original #1234 open.
cause: paged() treats an empty page as the end of the listing, so a transient empty third page of the fork's ~280 mirrors dropped the oldest 41; mirror.py saw them as unmirrored and created the oldest 40 (its cap). Separately, by_up kept the first mirror seen per upstream issue, and the listing is newest first, so a duplicate shadowed the original.
insight: The run summary settled it: upstream_open 192 with exactly the 41 lowest numbers missing is a truncated tail, not an empty listing. Mirrors are created oldest first, so a missing upstream issue older than the newest mirrored one is itself the signal that the listing was short; the guard refuses (exit 1, a red run) instead of guessing. The same day the triage board script hit an empty listing too and created a second board, so treat any empty or short GitHub listing as suspect. Control: the original script fails the transient-page, short-listing, empty-listing and duplicate-tracking scenarios in test_mirror.py; the fixed one passes all seven.
